script.speaker: M1
script.text: Have you finished reading the novel for our literature class?

script.speaker: W1
script.text: I'm only halfway through, and the discussion is tomorrow!

options: She has not finished the novel yet.
She enjoyed the second half of the novel.
The discussion has been moved to next week.
She will lead the discussion tomorrow.
questions.key_sentence: I'm only halfway through, and the discussion is tomorrow!
questions.key_translation_id: Saya baru setengah jalan, padahal diskusinya besok!
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: fokus pada kalimat wanita (orang kedua). Langkah 2: 'only halfway through' berarti baru membaca setengah. Jadi ia belum selesai membaca novel itu.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: focus on the woman, the second speaker. Step 2: 'only halfway through' means she has read only half. So she hasn't finished the novel.

why_wrong_id.1: Ia baru setengah, jadi belum membaca paruh kedua. 'Half' adalah jebakan kata yang mirip.
why_wrong_id.2: Ia justru menegaskan diskusinya besok, bukan dipindah.
why_wrong_id.3: Ia tidak menyebut akan memimpin diskusi.

why_wrong_en.1: She's only halfway, so she hasn't read the second half. 'Half' is a look-alike trap.
why_wrong_en.2: She says the discussion is tomorrow; it hasn't moved.
why_wrong_en.3: She never says she'll lead it.

questions.analogy_id: 'Halfway through' itu seperti mendaki gunung dan baru sampai pos tengah: puncaknya masih jauh.
questions.analogy_en: 'Halfway through' is like reaching the middle camp on a mountain: the summit is still far away.
questions.tip_id: Kata 'only' sering menandakan 'belum cukup'. Dengarkan nada khawatir di kalimat kedua.
questions.tip_en: 'Only' often signals 'not enough yet'. Listen for worry in the second line.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: This printer keeps jamming every time I try to print my essay.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Why don't you email it to me? Mine works fine.

options: Printing the essay on his printer.
Buying new paper for the printer.
questions.key_sentence: Why don't you email it to me? Mine works fine.
questions.key_translation_id: Kenapa tidak kamu kirim lewat email ke saya? Punya saya berfungsi baik.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'Why don't you…?' adalah saran. Langkah 2: pria meminta esai dikirim kepadanya dan berkata 'Mine works fine' (printer saya lancar). Jadi esai dicetak dengan printer milik pria.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'Why don't you…?' is a suggestion. Step 2: he asks her to email the essay and says 'Mine works fine', meaning his printer. So the essay gets printed on his printer.

why_wrong_id.0: Ia tidak menawarkan memperbaiki printer, tetapi memakai printernya sendiri.
why_wrong_id.3: Kertas tidak disebut; masalahnya printer macet.

why_wrong_en.0: He doesn't offer to fix it; he offers his own printer.
why_wrong_en.3: Paper isn't mentioned; the printer is jamming.

questions.analogy_id: 'Mine' itu seperti berkata 'pakai payungku saja': kata ganti milik menunjukkan siapa yang menolong.
questions.analogy_en: 'Mine' is like saying 'use my umbrella': the possessive shows who is helping.
questions.tip_id: Perhatikan kata milik (mine, yours) di kalimat kedua; sering menjadi kunci siapa yang melakukan apa.
questions.tip_en: Notice possessives (mine, yours) in the second line; they often show who does what.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: I heard the campus gym is free for students this month.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: Tell me about it! I've been there every day this week.

options: She wants the man to explain the offer.
She already knows and has been using the gym.
She has not been to the gym this week.
She thinks the gym is too expensive.
questions.key_sentence: Tell me about it! I've been there every day this week.
questions.key_translation_id: Iya, betul sekali! Saya sudah ke sana setiap hari minggu ini.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'Tell me about it!' adalah idiom yang berarti 'betul sekali, aku tahu', bukan meminta penjelasan. Langkah 2: kalimat berikutnya menguatkan: ia sudah ke gym setiap hari minggu ini. Jadi ia sudah tahu dan sudah memakai gym.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'Tell me about it!' is an idiom meaning 'I know, absolutely', not a request for details. Step 2: the next sentence confirms she's been every day this week.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini arti harfiah 'tell me about it'. Dalam percakapan, idiom ini berarti setuju/sudah tahu. Jebakan kata yang sama.
why_wrong_id.2: Kebalikan dari audio: ia ke gym setiap hari.
why_wrong_id.3: Gym itu gratis bulan ini, dan ia tidak mengeluh soal harga.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the literal meaning. In conversation the idiom means 'I know'. Same-word trap.
why_wrong_en.2: The opposite: she's been every day.
why_wrong_en.3: The gym is free this month, and she doesn't complain about cost.

questions.analogy_id: Idiom itu seperti kode rahasia antar teman: 'Tell me about it' bukan minta cerita, tapi 'aku juga mengalaminya'.
questions.analogy_en: Idioms are friends' secret codes: 'Tell me about it' isn't asking for a story; it means 'I know exactly'.
questions.tip_id: Kalau pilihan terdengar seperti arti harfiah idiom, hati-hati, biasanya jebakan.
questions.tip_en: If an option sounds like the idiom's literal meaning, be careful; it's usually the trap.

items.prompt: Bamboo grows ______ than most other plants, sometimes adding nearly a meter in a single day.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: ada kata 'than' setelah rumpang, tanda perbandingan dua hal (comparative, bentuk perbandingan lebih). Langkah 2: 'fast' adalah kata pendek, jadi comparative-nya ditambah -er: **faster**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'than' follows the blank, which signals a comparative. Step 2: 'fast' is a short word, so its comparative takes -er: **faster**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'fast' bentuk biasa; tidak bisa dipasangkan dengan 'than'.
why_wrong_id.1: 'fastest' adalah superlative (bentuk paling), dipakai dengan 'the', bukan 'than'.
why_wrong_id.2: Kata pendek satu suku kata tidak memakai 'more'. 'More fast' salah.

why_wrong_en.1: 'fastest' is a superlative used with 'the', not 'than'.
why_wrong_en.2: One-syllable words don't use 'more'; 'more fast' is wrong.

items.analogy_id: Comparative itu adu dua pelari: 'than' adalah garis finis yang menunjukkan siapa lawannya.
items.analogy_en: A comparative is a two-runner race: 'than' is the finish line naming the rival.
items.tip_id: Lihat 'than'? Cari bentuk -er atau more + adjective.
items.tip_en: See 'than'? Look for -er or more + adjective.

items.prompt: The committee ______ its decision after the final meeting next Monday.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: cari penanda waktu: 'next Monday' (Senin depan) menunjukkan masa depan. Langkah 2: tense (bentuk waktu) untuk masa depan adalah will + V1: **will announce**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: find the time marker: 'next Monday' points to the future. Step 2: the future tense is will + base verb: **will announce**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'announced' adalah bentuk lampau, bertentangan dengan 'next Monday'.
why_wrong_id.2: 'has announced' (present perfect) berarti sudah terjadi, tidak cocok dengan masa depan.
why_wrong_id.3: 'announcing' tanpa auxiliary (kata kerja bantu) bukan verb utama.

why_wrong_en.2: 'has announced' means it already happened; it doesn't fit the future.
why_wrong_en.3: 'announcing' without an auxiliary isn't a main verb.

items.analogy_id: Penanda waktu itu seperti kalender di dinding: lihat dulu tanggalnya, baru pilih bentuk kata kerja.
items.analogy_en: Time markers are the wall calendar: check the date first, then pick the verb form.
items.tip_id: Cari kata waktu (yesterday, next, since, already) sebelum memilih tense.
items.tip_en: Find the time word (yesterday, next, since, already) before choosing a tense.

items.prompt: Each of the {A}volunteers{/A} {B}were{/B} given a {C}map{/C} of the {D}area{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: subject (pelaku) sebenarnya adalah 'Each', bukan 'volunteers'. Langkah 2: 'Each' selalu tunggal, dan frasa 'of the volunteers' tidak mengubahnya. Jadi verb (kata kerja) harus tunggal: **was** given.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: the real subject is 'Each', not 'volunteers'. Step 2: 'Each' is always singular, and 'of the volunteers' doesn't change that. So the verb must be singular: **was** given.

why_wrong_id.0: Setelah 'each of the' memang memakai noun (kata benda) jamak: 'volunteers'. Benar.
why_wrong_id.2: 'a map' adalah noun tunggal yang tepat setelah article (kata sandang) 'a'.

why_wrong_en.0: 'each of the' is correctly followed by a plural noun: 'volunteers'.
why_wrong_en.2: 'a map' is a correct singular noun after 'a'.

items.analogy_id: 'Each' itu satu kursi sopir. Frasa 'of the volunteers' hanya daftar penumpang di belakang; yang menyetir tetap satu orang.
items.analogy_en: 'Each' is one driver's seat; 'of the volunteers' is just the passenger list. Only one person is driving.
items.tip_id: Coret frasa 'of …', lalu cocokkan verb dengan kata sebelum 'of'.
items.tip_en: Cross out the 'of …' phrase, then match the verb to the word before 'of'.

items.prompt: The museum's new exhibit {A}has attracted{/A} {B}thousands{/B} of visitors {C}since{/C} it {D}open{/D} in May.
items.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: 'in May' menunjuk waktu lampau yang spesifik. Langkah 2: setelah 'since', kejadian titik awalnya memakai simple past (V2). Jadi 'open' harus menjadi **opened**.
items.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'in May' is a specific past time. Step 2: after 'since', the starting event uses the simple past (V2). So 'open' should be **opened**.

why_wrong_id.0: 'has attracted' (present perfect) tepat dengan 'since': dampaknya berlanjut sampai sekarang.
why_wrong_id.1: 'thousands of visitors' adalah pola yang benar.
why_wrong_id.2: 'since' tepat untuk titik awal waktu bersama present perfect.

why_wrong_en.2: 'since' correctly marks the starting point with the present perfect.

items.analogy_id: 'Since' itu pita garis start. Pita itu dipasang di masa lalu (opened), sementara pelarinya masih berlari sampai sekarang (has attracted).
items.analogy_en: 'Since' is the starting ribbon, set in the past (opened), while the runners keep going to now (has attracted).
items.tip_id: Pola: present perfect + since + simple past.
items.tip_en: Pattern: present perfect + since + simple past.

items.title: The Return of the Bicycle
items.body:
In many cities around the world, bicycles are returning to streets that were designed almost entirely for cars. City governments have discovered that encouraging cycling can solve several problems at once.

The first advantage is space. A single car lane can carry far more people per hour when it is turned into a protected bicycle lane, because bicycles are small and travel close together. Cities that once struggled with traffic jams have found that adding cycle lanes keeps people moving without the expense of building new roads. Some have even closed busy streets to cars on weekends.

Health is another reason for the change. Regular cycling strengthens the heart and lungs, and people who ride to work tend to take fewer sick days. Because bicycles produce no exhaust, **they** also improve air quality for everyone, including people who never ride.

Bike-sharing programs have made cycling even more **accessible**. Users can unlock a bicycle with a phone, ride it across town, and leave it at another station. Visitors and residents who do not own a bicycle can therefore travel cheaply and easily.

Not everyone welcomed the change at first. Some shop owners worried that removing parking spaces would reduce the number of customers. However, studies in several cities found that cyclists visit local shops more often than drivers do, even if they spend slightly less on each visit. Over time, many business owners have become supporters of cycle lanes.

The bicycle, an invention more than two hundred years old, is once again shaping the future of city life.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Car lanes are wider than bicycle lanes.
Cities are encouraging cycling because it brings many benefits.
Shop owners prefer customers who drive.
questions.evidence_quote: City governments have discovered that encouraging cycling can solve several problems at once.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: paragraf 1 menyebut kota-kota mendorong bersepeda karena bisa menyelesaikan beberapa masalah sekaligus. Langkah 2: paragraf berikutnya merinci manfaat itu (ruang, kesehatan, bike-sharing, dampak ke toko). Jadi ide pokoknya kota mendorong bersepeda karena banyak manfaat.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: paragraph 1 says cities encourage cycling because it solves several problems at once. Step 2: later paragraphs list those benefits (space, health, bike-sharing, shops). So that's the main idea.

why_wrong_id.1: Lebar jalur tidak dibandingkan; yang dibahas jumlah orang per jam.
why_wrong_id.3: Kebalikan dari teks: pesepeda justru lebih sering berbelanja di toko lokal.

why_wrong_en.1: Lane width isn't compared; people per hour is.
why_wrong_en.3: The opposite: cyclists visit local shops more often.

questions.analogy_id: Main idea itu tujuan akhir perjalanan; detail adalah halte-halte yang dilewati.
questions.analogy_en: The main idea is the journey's destination; details are the stops along the way.
questions.tip_id: Cari kalimat yang 'menjanjikan' isi teks: 'several problems at once' → teks akan menyebut masalah-masalah itu.
questions.tip_en: Look for the sentence that 'promises' the content: 'several problems at once' means they'll be listed.

questions.prompt: The word **they** in paragraph 3 refers to
questions.evidence_quote: Because bicycles produce no exhaust, they also improve air quality for everyone, including people who never ride.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kalimatnya: 'Because bicycles produce no exhaust, they also improve air quality…'. Langkah 2: yang tidak menghasilkan asap dan memperbaiki kualitas udara adalah sepeda. Ganti: '**bicycles** also improve air quality'. Cocok.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: 'Because bicycles produce no exhaust, they also improve air quality…'. Step 2: what produces no exhaust and improves the air? Bicycles. Substitute: '**bicycles** also improve air quality'. It fits.

why_wrong_id.1: 'people' disebut di akhir kalimat sebagai yang ikut merasakan udara bersih, bukan penyebabnya.
why_wrong_id.2: 'sick days' (hari sakit) tidak bisa memperbaiki udara.
why_wrong_id.3: Jantung dan paru-paru ada di kalimat sebelumnya dan tidak memperbaiki kualitas udara kota.

why_wrong_en.1: 'people' appears later as those who benefit, not the cause.
why_wrong_en.3: The heart and lungs are in the previous sentence and don't clean city air.

questions.analogy_id: Pronoun 'they' itu anak panah yang menunjuk ke belakang; ikuti arahnya ke noun jamak terdekat yang masuk akal.
questions.analogy_en: 'They' is an arrow pointing back; follow it to the nearest plural noun that makes sense.
questions.tip_id: Pronoun di clause induk sering merujuk ke subject clause 'because' di depannya.
questions.tip_en: A pronoun in the main clause often refers to the subject of the 'because' clause before it.

questions.prompt: The word **accessible** in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: Visitors and residents who do not own a bicycle can therefore travel cheaply and easily.
questions.why_correct_id: Langkah 1: kalimat sesudahnya menjelaskan: orang yang tidak punya sepeda pun bisa bepergian dengan murah dan mudah. Langkah 2: sesuatu yang bisa dipakai siapa saja dengan mudah berarti mudah didapat/tersedia. Jadi 'accessible' ≈ **available**.
questions.why_correct_en: Step 1: the next sentences explain that even people without bikes can travel cheaply and easily. Step 2: something anyone can easily use is available. So 'accessible' ≈ **available**.

why_wrong_id.0: Tidak ada petunjuk bahaya; konteksnya justru kemudahan.
why_wrong_id.2: 'popular' (populer) mungkin benar di dunia nyata, tetapi konteks menekankan kemudahan memakai, bukan jumlah penggemar.
why_wrong_id.3: Teknologi ponsel disebut, tetapi kata itu menggambarkan kemudahan, bukan kemodernan.

why_wrong_en.0: No sign of danger; the context is about ease.
why_wrong_en.2: 'popular' may be true in life, but the context stresses ease of use, not fans.
why_wrong_en.3: Phones are mentioned, but the word describes ease, not modernity.

questions.analogy_id: Konteks itu seperti cahaya di ruangan gelap: kalimat sebelum dan sesudah menerangi arti kata yang belum kamu kenal.
questions.analogy_en: Context is the light in a dark room: the sentences around a word reveal its meaning.
questions.tip_id: Jangan memilih arti yang 'benar di dunia nyata'; pilih yang cocok dengan kalimat di teks.
questions.tip_en: Don't pick what's 'true in real life'; pick what fits the sentence in the text.
